ageing_relevance.rationale: TIMP1 is one of the seven GrimAge plasma-protein surrogates, and the ageing share of its papers is moderate (21%). Its age-related disease associations are broad but low-scoring (≤0.12). It did not differ significantly in the schizophrenia meta-analysis main model, and the GrimAge surrogates are methylation estimates, not measured protein.

evidence.value: One of seven plasma proteins whose DNA-methylation surrogates make up GrimAge, the mortality clock that was +4.3 years older in schizophrenia in part 1 of this project (an effect explained by smoking). The surrogates are methylation estimates, not measured protein levels. Not significantly different in the main model of Shirai et al. 2024's meta-analysis.

background_knowledge: Circulating TIMP1 is elevated in ageing and cardiovascular disease, and higher TIMP1 predicts mortality in cohort studies.

mechanism.rationale: TIMP1 is a well-characterised MMP inhibitor and also has growth-factor signalling through CD63 and ITGB1. Its direction in ageing is unclear, because the MMP-inhibitory and signalling roles may act in opposite directions, and raised plasma levels are a marker of risk.

evidence.value: Metalloproteinase inhibitor that functions by forming one to one complexes with target metalloproteinases, such as collagenases, and irreversibly inactivates them by binding to their catalytic zinc cofactor.

background_knowledge: Higher TIMP1 may be a compensatory response to tissue remodelling, so the causal direction is uncertain.

tractability.rationale: There is no small-molecule or other-modality evidence. Only antibody tractability (secreted protein) and a PROTAC ubiquitination flag are reported, and a secreted inhibitor is difficult to modulate selectively.

safety.rationale: Two liabilities are listed, both generic gene-regulation terms. Inhibiting a broad MMP inhibitor may promote matrix degradation, and TIMP1 has roles in cancer and fibrosis. There is little specific safety data.
background_knowledge: Broad MMP inhibition in the clinic caused musculoskeletal toxicity. TIMP1 is implicated in tumour progression.

clinical_precedence.rationale: No drugs are listed for TIMP1. As a secreted protein, any drugs acting on its targets (MMPs) would not be listed here.

assessment.summary: TIMP1 is a secreted MMP inhibitor with growth-factor activity. It is a GrimAge plasma-protein surrogate, but it was not significantly different in the schizophrenia meta-analysis main model. Its ageing literature share is moderate (21%), and its age-related disease associations are broad but weak. It has only antibody-type tractability and no clinical candidates. The direction of modulation is unclear, because elevated TIMP1 is a risk marker that may be compensatory. I recommend deprioritising it, and using it as a biomarker rather than a drug target for now.
key_uncertainties: Whether raising or lowering TIMP1 would slow ageing; elevated levels may be compensatory rather than causal
GrimAge surrogates are methylation estimates, not measured protein
Safety profile is generic; MMP-pathway modulation and cancer roles are not captured by the tool
